parts.answer: The two sides reduce to the same expression.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ or $\tan\theta\cos\theta=\sin\theta$ appropriately at least once. M1. Use $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$ or $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$ appropriately. M1. These two marks may be applied in reverse order; after an error no further marks. Work may proceed from either side. If both sides are worked simultaneously, maximum M1M1 only if a common correct expression is reached. If numerator and denominator are worked separately, bring them together for the second mark. Fully correct proof. A1 WWW. Condone missing brackets if recovered. Total: 3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use part (a) and eliminate fractions: $\frac{\tan\theta+7}{\tan^2\theta-3}=\frac5{\tan\theta}$, hence $\tan\theta(\tan\theta+7)=5(\tan^2\theta-3)$. *B1 OE. Factorise or otherwise solve their 3-term quadratic: $4\tan^2\theta-7\tan\theta-15=0$, so $(4\tan\theta+5)(\tan\theta-3)=0$. DM1; condone errors forming the quadratic. $\tan\theta=-1.25$ and $\tan\theta=3$. B1 OE, independent of factorisation and no extra solutions; may be implied by a correct final answer. $\theta=71.6^\circ$ and $128.7^\circ$. B1 AWRT; no others in range; ignore answers outside range. Maximum 3/4 if factorisation or formula is incorrect. Total: 4.
